prompt:
A line-art multi-panel storyboard of one continuous scene of a live-action short drama: one image divided into a grid of 3 columns and 3 rows of equal 9:16 panels, 9 panels read from left to right and top to bottom; cells after the last panel stay plain white. Every panel is a clean, simple line drawing: uniform thin black outlines on a plain white background, with no shading, hatching, grey tones, colour or texture. Each panel has a thin black border, with plain white gutters between the panels. Location: Garden of the wedding venue, Day, bright warm sunlight from high on the right.
Image 1: the character sheet of Natalie (25), look S1
Image 2: the character sheet of George (55), look S1
Image 3: the character sheet of Lauren (50), look S1
Image 4: the location Garden of the wedding venue, the front view, the establishing view, facing the back wall, with no people
Image 5: the location Garden of the wedding venue, the back view, turned 180 degrees, facing the front wall, with the left wall at its right edge, with no people
Image 6: the location Garden of the wedding venue, the left-side view, facing the left wall, with the back wall at its right edge, with no people
Image 7: the location Garden of the wedding venue, the right-side view, facing the right wall, with the back wall at its left edge, with no people
Image 8: the location Garden of the wedding venue, the floor plan seen from above: its top edge is the back wall, its bottom edge the front wall behind the front view's camera, and its left and right edges the left and right walls, with no people
Image 9: the blocking reference of this segment, the same place with its people in their places at the start; use it only for where each person is and which way they face, and keep each person on that seat or spot, on the same side of the room, in every panel until a shot moves them; do not copy its colours or light
Image 10: the prop bouquet; use only structure, material, and color
Image 11: the prop glasses of champagne; use only structure, material, and color
Draw each character so they can be told apart as in their reference image: the hairstyle, build and outfit in outline. Use the character sheets only for the characters, not for their layout, white background or multiple views. Use the location images only for the layout of the space and the place of its furniture and props, drawn in outline. There is only one of each vehicle, piece of furniture and prop that the location shows, defined by the location images, throughout all panels; when a panel shows only part of one, such as a car's hood, it is that same object, and no second one appears. Each panel shows only the characters it names, and nobody appears twice in one panel.
At the start: Sunny day in the wedding garden. There is one white wooden wedding arch with sheer white drapes and white flower garlands at the far end of the aisle runner. Two short rows of white folding chairs face the arch, one row on each side of the aisle. There is one small round white cocktail table in front of the boxwood hedge, holding one silver tray of champagne flutes. Natalie stands under the centre of the arch, facing down the aisle, holding the bouquet at her waist in both hands. George stands beside her under the arch on the rose-bush side, facing down the aisle. The boxwood-hedge side of the arch beside Natalie is empty. Lauren stands at the head of the aisle beside the front row of chairs on the boxwood-hedge side, turned toward the arch. Guest 1 and Guest 2 stand at the cocktail table, Guest 1 on the arch side of it and Guest 2 on the aisle side, each holding a champagne flute. Cassie stands at the end of the front row of chairs on the rose-bush side, by the stone garden wall, arms crossed. Sebastian has not arrived. The camera is on the aisle in front of the arch, on the rose-bush side of the aisle.
Panel 1: Close-up insert, locked-off camera, eye-level. Tall crystal flutes of pale golden champagne stand on the silver tray on the white cocktail table, catching the sunlight, with the boxwood hedge out of focus behind them.
Panel 2: Wide shot, slow push in toward the arch from the middle of the aisle, low angle, the arch centred. Natalie stands under the flower-hung arch with the bouquet and George stands beside her on the rose-bush side. The space on her other side is empty. Lauren stands at the front row of chairs in the foreground, turned toward them.
Panel 3: Medium two-shot, locked-off camera, eye-level. Under the arch, George turns toward Natalie with a nervous, placating smile and pats her arm once.
Panel 4: Medium close-up, clean single of Natalie, tight on face and shoulders, eye-level. Natalie turns her face to George, her eyes steady and serious above the veil.
Panel 5: Medium shot, dirty single of George with Natalie's shoulder and veil at the frame edge, eye-level. George drops his gaze and glances toward Lauren at the front row, avoiding his daughter's eyes.
Panel 6: Close-up insert, high angle on the wrist. Lauren turns her wrist and checks her slim gold wristwatch with an impatient tap of one finger.
Panel 7: Medium shot, locked-off camera, eye-level, Lauren in three-quarter profile at the front row. Lauren lowers her wrist and looks up at Natalie under the arch with a cold, bored smile.
Panel 8: Close-up, clean single of Natalie, slow push in, eye-level. Natalie holds Lauren's gaze, and her fingers tighten around the bouquet's ribbon-wrapped stems.
Panel 9: Medium close-up, clean single of Lauren, low angle. Lauren arches one brow and gives a thin, dismissive smile toward the arch.
Keep the characters, the number and position of every vehicle, piece of furniture and prop, and the location's spatial orientation consistent across all panels.
No text, letters, numbers, captions, speech bubbles, panel labels or watermark anywhere in the image; no photographic rendering, shading or colour.
